Slot table covers the 2 Phase 3 primary slots (`inventory_quick_view`, `action_prompt`, category `hud_widgets`) plus 5 chrome supporting slots (`compass_rose`, `depth_indicator`, `gold_counter`, `champion_bar_frame`, `action_strip_frame`, category `hud_chrome`). The default state (no manifest file present) keeps the existing procedural-rectangle fallback in `src/dm2/dm2_v2_hud_overlay.c` — `uses_placeholder()` returns 1 for every slot, the gate reports `NO_MANIFEST`, and the V1 invariant is preserved. Promotion to `PARTIAL`/`COMPLETE` requires operator-installed manifest + per-slot real `source_file` entries with `generator != "placeholder"` plus the actual on-disk art; finished PBR widget bitmap art is still an OPEN-BOUNDED gap. - 2026-07-23 DM2-008 audible playback backend (Lane B, cycle 16):
  Implemented voice allocation, PCM decode, and a real SDL3 playback backend
  behind the existing fail-closed contract (skproject SKWIN/SkwinSDL.cpp
  OpenAudio/sdlAudMix, MAX_SB = 16, PLAYBACK_FREQUENCY = 6000 Hz;
  SKULLWIN/c_sound.cpp:256-308 R_928 metric).
  Changes:
    * `src/dm2/dm2_v1_sound.c` / `include/dm2_v1_sound.h`:
      - `dm2_v1_sound_decode_gdat_pcm()` /
        `dm2_v1_sound_gdat_pcm_sample_count()`: decode a verified GDAT sound
        raw entry into unsigned 8-bit mono PCM at 6000 Hz.  The payload is
        the raw entry after the two-byte format header, converted
        `byte ^ 0x80` — the same conversion as
        `dm2_v1_gdat_sound_toggle_payload()` / SKWin's `0x80 + raw_byte`.
        Verified against the local canonical GRAPHICS.DAT: 292 loadable
        SOUND entries, byte-exact decode of entry 3/0/129.
      - Voice allocation: 16 module-owned voice slots (SKWin `MAX_SB`),
        first-free allocation, voices free when the backend reports
        completion, no stealing; the 17th simultaneous request is rejected
        explicitly (`rejected_no_free_voice`).
      - `dm2_v1_sound_bind_playback_backend()`: binds an SDL-free playback
        vtable (open/is_ready/start_voice/voice_active/stop_all/close).
      - `dm2_v1_sound_play_gdat_entry()` /
        `dm2_v1_sound_play_gdat_entry_positional()`: audible playback only
        when the sample decodes from a verified GDAT entry and the backend
        reports ready; effective volume is the source-locked R_928
        attenuation byte (dx == dy == 0 keeps full volume), never
        synthesized.
      - `dm2_v1_sound_play()` / `dm2_v1_sound_play_positional()`: the
        sound_id is now the GDAT raw sample binding (xsndptr2 `w_00`),
        resolved back to the owning SOUND entry before decode; -1 stays
        explicit without loader, backend, or a matching entry.
      - Title music stays fail-closed: no verified music asset root is
        proven locally (no `SKWIN/data/*.hmp.mid` assets present).
    * `src/dm2/dm2_v1_sound_sdl_backend.c` /
      `include/dm2_v1_sound_sdl_backend.h` (new): concrete SDL3 backend —
      6000 Hz U8 mono `SDL_OpenAudioDeviceStream`, additive sdlAudMix-shaped
      per-voice mixing with clamping, thread-safe voice table
      (`SDL_LockAudioStream`), observability counters for probes.
    * `CMakeLists.txt`: new `test_dm2_v1_sound_playback_sdl` target/CTest
      (SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy); `firestaff_dm2` now links SDL3::SDL3 publicly
      because its `src/dm2/dm2_v1_*.c` glob picked up the new backend.
    * `tests/test_dm2_v1_sound_gdat_real_data.c`: added PCM-decode checks
      (sample count, query-only hash, capacity rejection, byte-exact
      payload ^ 0x80, unknown-entry rejection) and no-backend playback
      rejection checks.
    * `tests/test_dm2_v1_sound_playback_sdl.c` (new): real-data audible
      playback proof — voice start/completion, mixed-frame progress, legacy
      sound_id routing, R_928 positional attenuation, 16-voice exhaustion,
      stop_all and slot reuse.  Skips cleanly without local data.
    * `tests/test_dm2_v1_sound_source_gate.c`: fail-closed decode/playback
      checks without loader/backend.
    * `probes/firestaff_dm2_v1_creature_combat_probe.c`: unchanged; the
      fail-closed assertions still hold (158/158 PASS).
  Verification: `ctest --test-dir build -R dm2_v1_sound` 4/4 PASS
  (queue_pc34_compat, source_gate, gdat_real_data, playback_sdl);
  `firestaff_dm2_v1_creature_combat_probe` 158/158 PASS.  No new failures
  introduced elsewhere.
  Remaining: app-side backend binding in the M11 DM2 runtime path, a
  verified music asset root before the title cue can play, and proven
  wall-occlusion/facing routing for positional cues.

        CREATURES word fields 0x0A..0x14 from a verified GDAT loader and
        resolves them in source order (skcrture.cpp:2092-2100

        defense provider (same pattern as the CAII word providers);
        `dm2_v1_combat_resolve_attack_on_creature()` resolves the source
        damage formula against the creature's AIDefinition Defense byte @8

        origin cell, decrements its byte@4 duration, requeues every

  `0x5e` summon in `src/dm2/dm2_v1_spell_timer_handlers_pc34_compat.c`, with
  declarations in `include/dm2_v1_spell_timer_handlers_pc34_compat.h`:
    * Cloud handler records the origin cell and object effect and fails closed
      on DB14 record mutation until a real cloud owner is proven.
    * Missile handler maps `DM2_OBJECT_EFFECT_*` to a DM2 projectile subtype and
      dispatches a live projectile via
      `dm2_v1_projectile_dispatch_synthetic`; unmapped effects are rejected.
    * Summon handler records the origin cell and fails closed on synthetic DB4
      creature record creation.
    * Added `dm2_v1_spell_timer_object_effect_to_projectile_subtype()` and
      `dm2_v1_spell_timer_dispatch()` helpers.
  Wired all spell-effect handlers into the live `src/dm2/dm2_v1_runtime.c`
  `dm2_v1_proceed_timers` dispatch via `dm2_runtime_spell_timer_wrapper()`,
  keeping the dispatcher's main context as `DM2_V1_RuntimeState` for
  door/actuator/weather handlers and refreshing the spell-handler context each
  tick with the current game tick, map, and (when available) record pools /
  dungeon / CAII data. Added runtime M11 DM2 status-scope accessors
  (`dm2_v1_runtime_note_spell_cast_apply_receipt()`,
  `dm2_v1_runtime_status_scope()`, `dm2_v1_runtime_status_message()`,
  `dm2_v1_runtime_last_spell_failure_class()`) in `src/dm2/dm2_v1_runtime.c`.
  Also fixed a build-blocking typedef redefinition between
  `include/theron_v1_combat.h` and `include/theron_v1_world.h` by forward-
  typedef-ing `Theron_V1_World` in `theron_v1_world.h` before including
  `theron_v1_combat.h`.
  Tests:
    * Extended `tests/test_dm2_v1_spell_cast_player_pc34_compat.c` with focused
      checks for cloud fail-closed behaviour, fireball projectile dispatch,
      unknown-object-effect rejection, and summon fail-closed behaviour
      (134/134 checks pass).

    * `skproject/SKULLWIN/c_tim_proc.cpp:4268-4280`
      DM2_ALLOC_NEW_CREATURE (0x5e)

        turning, and OOB/map-edge blocking (west/north boundaries).

        level geometry is connected and playable.
      - Reports when the current Structure1B decoder yields zero in-bounds wall
        squares (real LEV00 decodes as 4095 floor + 1 door with the existing
        0x0FFF collision-ref wall rule) and falls back to OOB blocking checks.

# ✅ 2026-07-14 DM2 G1 direct DB4 live-instance GDAT ownership

The V1 viewport now carries the original DB4 ObjectID from the dungeon record
into each direct-creature sprite plan. A `CREATURES/type/F9` draw is admitted
only when the active G1 receipt matches that exact ObjectID, source tile,
creature type, decoded dimensions, and local-palette hash. A same-type
creature elsewhere in the source corpus cannot authorize the draw. Missing or
mismatched instance receipts block the source-required creature pass without a
generic fallback. Source: SKProject `SKWIN/DME.h::Creature::CreatureType()`;
`SKWIN/c_map.cpp::QUERY_DUNGEON_MAP_CHIP_PICT`; and
  `SKWIN/SkWinCore.cpp::DRAW_CHIP_OF_MAGIC_MAP`. Verification: external build
  targets `test_dm2_v1_g1_scene_viewport_material_gate` and
  `test_dm2_v1_g1_creature_material_graph_gate`; direct runs and CTest 2/2 pass.

- ✅ 2026-07-14 DM1 PC34 external-save HoC runtime gate: every
  operator-staged, checksum-qualified PC34 corpus candidate now has a
  fixture-free M11 F0435 runtime check against original DM1 media. The gate
  compares the adopted live party pose/tick and owned dungeon with an
  independently materialized F0435 world, requires a nonblank M11 frame, and
  rejects a fabricated transient C040/HoC panel. Source-lock: ReDMCSB
  `LOADSAVE.C F0435` and `REVIVE.C F0280/F0282`. Verification: CTest
  `dm1_v1_original_save_pc34_external_hoc_runtime` (skip-safe without an
  operator corpus or original media).

- ✅ 2026-07-06 boot-probe level-loaded gate and Nexus selected-entry isolation: CLI/API `--boot-probe-expect-level-loaded <0|1>` / `bootProbeExpectLevelLoaded` now fail when a boot receipt is in the wrong level-materialization state. The all-games selected-entry gate now proves CSB and Nexus title startup phases keep a loaded level behind active startup while runtime is frozen, and Theron's initial startup phase remains level-unloaded until its forcefield/runtime handoff. M11 Nexus new selected-entry boots now also reset the reused launcher singleton's game tick, mechanics state, and champion party before showing the title, so a prior Nexus runtime probe cannot leak Syra/party state or nonzero ticks into a fresh title boot. Verification: `cmake --build build-codex-boot-local --target firestaff test_m11_direct_launch_prepare_all_games --parallel 4`, `ctest --test-dir build-codex-boot-local -R '^m11_direct_launch_prepare_all_games$' -V --timeout 140`, `cmake --build build-codex-boot-local --target test_m11_nexus_startup_gate test_nexus_v1_m11_launcher_handoff_boundary --parallel 4`, `ctest --test-dir build-codex-boot-local -R '^(m11_nexus_startup_gate|nexus_v1_m11_launcher_handoff_boundary)$' -V --timeout 140`, `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy ./build-codex-boot-local/firestaff --boot-probe --game theron --data-dir "$HOME/.firestaff/data" --boot-probe-frames 2 --boot-probe-expect-phase theron-startup-0 --boot-probe-expect-startup-active 1 --boot-probe-expect-level-loaded 0 --boot-probe-expect-runtime-tick-max 0 --duration 0`, the same Theron CLI with `--boot-probe-expect-level-loaded 1` fails with the expected mismatch, `cmake --build build-codex-boot-local --target firestaff_m11_phase_a_probe --parallel 4`, and `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy ./build-codex-boot-local/firestaff_m11_phase_a_probe` passed.

- ✅ 2026-07-05 Theron startup stage/Soul Room/forcefield gate: added a bounded startup-flow model for Theron's Quest before visible UI wiring. The model follows the manual, dmweb, PC Engine Software Bible, and Dungeon Master forum evidence: choose an available stage, enter Soul Room, resurrect up to three heroes from seven mirrors, keep Theron as leader, reject duplicate mirrors and party overflow, and enter the central forcefield to materialize the selected party. The code also corrects misleading fixed-party comments in the Theron headers while keeping legacy save-unpack compatibility. - ✅ 2026-07-01 M11 input scale source-to-screen boundary gate: added the inverse helper `M11_MapSourcePointToPresentedForPresentation()` (declared in `include/main_loop_m11.h` next to its existing sibling, defined in `src/engine/m11_game_input_mapping.c`) used by touch overlay hit-tests, HUD button bounds, and mouse cursor positions on the presented surface. The new helper clamps the source coordinate to `[0..319] x [0..199]` **before** the `src * targetW` multiply so a caller-supplied out-of-range value (e.g. `1000000 * 3840 = 3.84e9`, beyond `INT_MAX`) cannot overflow on 4K V2.2 presentations; the post-multiply clamp then keeps the result inside `[0..targetW-1] x [0..targetH-1]`. Same target-extent resolution rules as the existing inverse: V1_ORIGINAL = passthrough / return 0, V20_FILTERED = always 640x400, V21_UPSCALED / V22_MODERN = user-selected with positive-extent requirement. New data-free CTest `m11_input_scale_boundary_source_to_screen_pc34_compat` (`tests/test_m11_input_scale_boundary_source_to_screen_pc34_compat.c` + CMakeLists.txt registration) pins five disjoint contracts: V20 ignores caller-supplied 4K extents (source center 160,100 lands on presented 320,200), V21/V22 zero or negative extents return 0 / leave x,y alone, composition `MapPresentedToSource ∘ MapSourceToPresented` equals identity on the source range within ±1 pixel across 7 sample points × 3 modes and a 10-resolution matrix for the geometric center (V21/V22 exact-identity round-trip), V1 passthrough at top-left / center / bottom-right, negative and overflow source clamp safely (V20 bottom-right via pre-multiply clamp, V21/V22 via the pre-multiply source clamp), 10-iteration determinism over V20/V21/V22, NULL output pointer safety, and explicit canaries at 1280x800 / 1920x1080 / 3840x2160 including V22 4K top-row y→0 and bottom-row y→2149 (199*2160/200 truncation, ±1 tolerance covers it via the symmetry round-trip). Source-locked against ReDMCSB `COMMAND.C:1379-1449 F0358` mouse-row scan, `COMMAND.C:1641-1660 F0359` primary click dispatch, `COORD.C:1903-1920` inclusive source zone expansion, and `src/engine/main_loop_m11.c` `m11_game_presentation_target` (line 145, the V20=640x400 / V21=selected / V22=selected routing used here). Disjoint from the existing `test_m11_input_scale_boundary_pc34_compat` (screen→framebuffer direction only), `test_dm1_v2_selected_resolution_input_mapping_pc34` (V21/V22 happy-path), `test_dm1_v2_4k_input_zone_mapping_pc34` (4K touch/HUD zone mapping), and `test_m11_display_aspect_present_rect` (presentation rect + 1920x1080 FIT integer-scale input). Verification: `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` clean configure, `cmake --build build --target test_m11_input_scale_boundary_source_to_screen_pc34_compat test_m11_input_scale_boundary_pc34_compat --parallel` clean under `-Wall -Wextra -O2` (no new warnings; pre-existing `m11_game_view.c` const-discard + unused-param warnings unchanged on this worktree), direct `./build/test_m11_input_scale_boundary_source_to_screen_pc34_compat` PASS 322/322 across 8 invariant groups, direct `./build/test_m11_input_scale_boundary_pc34_compat` PASS 222/222 (no regression on the sibling), focused CTest `^m11_input_scale_boundary_pc34_compat$|^m11_input_scale_boundary_source_to_screen_pc34_compat$` PASS 2/2, broader input/presentation regression set `m11_input_scale_boundary_pc34_compat|m11_input_scale_boundary_source_to_screen_pc34_compat|m11_input_queue_pc34_compat|m11_ui_scale|m11_display_aspect_present_rect|dm1_v2_selected_resolution_input_mapping_pc34|dm1_v2_4k_input_zone_mapping_pc34` PASS 7/7, and `git diff --check` clean. Honest scope: deterministic M11 source-to-screen math contract + new helper only; no live SDL event integration, no real game-data load, no screenshot, no original-game pixel parity claim, and the underlying gap list row "UI scaling + touch-target audit across launcher/game views" stays OPEN-LARGE (this commit adds the source-to-screen half of the M11 boundary but the broader launcher touch-target audit still requires follow-up). - ✅ 2026-06-29 DM1 V1 PC 3.4 native save LSV-02 per-game versioned manifest gate (gapbug_20260629_dm1_save_export_import_manifest_gate): extended `memory_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat` (LSV-01) with a 16-byte versioned manifest slot in `AdditionalData[0..15]` of the PC 3.4 `DM_SAVE_HEADER` — a region the original ReDMCSB engine never inspects, so vanilla DM 3.4 PC interop stays intact while Firestaff's importer gains a per-game compatibility gate. Manifest layout (LE, written into meta[41..48] in the obfuscated header half): `LSV01RDM` magic (8 bytes ASCII) + `formatVersion` (uint16, currently 1) + `gameCode` (uint16: 0x00D1=DM1, 0x00C5=CSB, 0x00D2=DM2, 0x00D9=NEXUS, 0x00D4=THERON) + `dungeonCode` (echoes `C10_DUNGEON_DM`) + reserved flags. The exporter (`F0795_SAVEGAME_ExportPC34_Compat`) now stamps the manifest with `gameCode=DM1` by default, the importer (`F0796_SAVEGAME_ImportPC34_Compat`) refuses any manifest with a non-DM1 gameCode (returns `SAVEGAME_PC34_ERROR_BAD_MAGIC`), and three new public helpers wire the per-game gate: `F0799_SAVEGAME_PC34PeekManifest_Compat` (manifest presence + version + gameCode + body size), `F0800_SAVEGAME_PC34ValidateGameCode_Compat(expectedGameCode, requireManifest)` (the per-game compatibility proof — strict mode rejects vanilla files, lenient mode accepts them for ReDMCSB interop), and `F0801_SAVEGAME_PC34GameCodeName_Compat` (stable ASCII names: DM1/CSB/DM2/NEXUS/THERON/UNSET/UNKNOWN). The importer stamps the parsed gameCode into the Firestaff `SaveGameHeader_Compat.reserved[5..6]` slot next to the existing GameID/MusicOn bytes, so the M12 launcher can quote the per-game verdict without re-parsing the PC 3.4 header. The CTest `test_dm1_v1_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat` (data-free, previously dormant in the tree) was registered in `CMakeLists.txt` and extended from 6 to 14 invariants: `cpsc_obfuscate_reversible` (F0417 reversible XOR), `header_round_trip` (F0795 + F0796 byte-stable), `bad_inputs_rejected` (NULL state, NULL outBuf, NULL party, small outBuf, short buf, NULL outState), `cpsc_layout` (header + 5 parts, LENGTH prefixes), `error_string_lookup` (F0797 string dispatch for both LSV-01 and LSV-02 codes), `format_id_tolerance` (vanilla PC 3.4 byte layout preserved), and eight new LSV-02 cases — `lsv02_manifest_present_and_valid`, `lsv02_per_game_gate_accepts_dm1`, `lsv02_per_game_gate_rejects_wrong_game` (hand-crafts a CSB manifest to prove the F0796 + F0800 verdict), `lsv02_vanilla_fallback` (zero-padded buffer + lenient/strict gate), `lsv02_magic_tampering` (zeroes the LSV01RDM magic in-place and re-obfuscates, asserts NOT_PRESENT), `lsv02_import_stamps_reserved_gamecode` (round-trip populates reserved[5..6] + DM1 gate OK), `lsv02_export_byte_stable` (two consecutive exports with the same input produce identical bytes; divergent gameID changes the bytes), and `lsv02_game_code_name_lookup`. Source-locked against ReDMCSB DEFS.H:468-480 (DM_SAVE_HEADER.GameID), DEFS.H:538-572 (GLOBAL_DATA.MusicOn), LOADSAVE.C F0433/F0435 (save/load chain), SAVEHEAD.C F0429/F0430 (header read/write with the C10_DM_SAVE_HEADER_DECRYPTION_KEY_INDEX obfuscation), READWRIT.C F0417 (CPSC checksum + reversible obfuscate), and the existing `memory_savegame_pc34_compat.h:227` (RDMCSB15 native magic). Disjoint from the existing `csb_v1_csbwin_save_loader_boundary_pc34_compat` (which gates the CSBWin dmsave/csbgame.dat path on 512-byte XOR/CSBWin 14-shape contract) and from the Theron `.srm` classifier (gzipped-deflate Save Disk manifest). Verification: `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` clean configure, `cmake --build build --target test_dm1_v1_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat --parallel` clean, `gcc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 -Iinclude -c src/memory/memory_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat.c` clean, `gcc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 -Iinclude -c tests/test_dm1_v1_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat.c` clean, direct `./build/test_dm1_v1_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat` PASS 14/14 (6 LSV-01 + 8 LSV-02), focused CTest `dm1_v1_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat` PASS 1/1, broader save/export/import CTest sweep (`savegame|save_browser|dm1_v1_savegame`) PASS 30/30 (no regressions in `save_browser_export_import_m12`, `dm1_v1_save_load_source_lock`, `pass607_dm1_v1_level_change_autosave_absence_source_lock`, `dm1_v1_save_load_slot_core`, `nexus_v1_save_slot_roundtrip_pc34_compat`, `nexus_v1_save_multislot_roundtrip_pc34_compat`, `csb_v1_csbwin_save_loader_boundary_pc34_compat_unit`, `csb_v1_csbwin_save_loader_boundary`, `nexus_v1_save_load_round_trip`, `theron_v1_save_load`, `theron_v1_save_header_rejection`, `theron_v1_save_progress_roundtrip_pc34`, `pass789_dm1_v1_mirror_candidate_c040_save_game_while_panel_live`), tier1 CTest sweep PASS 10/10, full project `cmake --build build` clean, `git diff --check` clean. Honest scope: LSV-01 byte-stable PC 3.4 export/import + LSV-02 per-game versioned manifest gate for the DM1 path; the CSB/DM2/Nexus/Theron manifest variants (different `gameCode` values via the same exporter contract) remain tracked under `docs/FIRESTAFF_GAP_LIST.md` `Save export/import` row, no real community-save import evidence, no per-game-version (Atari ST 1.x / Amiga 3.5 / Mac 1.2) byte-layout receipts, no end-to-end launcher save-browser wiring, and no M12 launch flow that consults the new strict per-game gate.

- ✅ 2026-06-28 M12 launcher cloud-sync opt-in boundary (gapbug_20260628_launcher_cloud_sync_boundary): bounded the existing `cloud_sync_m12` directory-based sync layer with an explicit launcher-owned opt-in gate and a conflict-safe no-op surface. The header now declares `M12_SYNC_OK_DISABLED` (clean return when opted out) and `M12_SYNC_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` (sync root missing / not a directory / not writable), plus `M12_CloudSync_SetEnabled/IsEnabled`, `M12_CloudSync_IsSyncRootUsable`, `M12_CloudSync_GetBoundaryTag` (stable tags `DISABLED` / `ENABLED_OK` / `ENABLED_NO_ROOT` / `ENABLED_NOT_A_DIR` / `ENABLED_UNWRITABLE`), and `M12_CloudSync_RunIfEnabled`. The implementation now: (1) defaults the opt-in flag to 0 (off) so the launcher is the single source of truth, (2) refuses bare relative paths and validates the sync root with `stat() + S_ISDIR + access(W_OK)` on every boundary check, (3) `RunIfEnabled` short-circuits to `M12_SYNC_OK_DISABLED` when off and to `M12_SYNC_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` when the root is unusable, never opening the manifest or touching tracked files, (4) `M12_CloudSync_ApplyConfig(const M12_Config*)` is the bounded wiring point that pushes `cloudSyncEnabled` + `cloudSyncDir` + `cloudSyncPolicy` into the runtime in one call, and (5) the existing `m12_apply_loaded_config` in `src/ui/menu_startup_m12.c` calls it right next to the `M11_HighContrast_SetActive` push so the boundary is hot on every launcher start. `M12_CloudSync_DiscoverSaveFiles(relativePrefix, absoluteDir)` now does a real bounded per-game `*.sav` directory walk (POSIX `opendir`/Win32 `FindFirstFile`, one level, `*.sav` only, idempotent on re-runs) and `m12_discover_tracked` calls it for `saves/{dm1,csb,dm2,nexus,theron}` instead of stubbing. The probe `probes/m12/firestaff_m12_cloud_sync_probe.c` was registered as CTest `m12_cloud_sync_boundary` and extended from 9 to 38 invariants covering: opt-in defaults disabled, `RunIfEnabled` is a strict no-op when off (no manifest file, zeroed stats, `M12_SYNC_OK_DISABLED`), `ENABLED_NOT_A_DIR` for a regular file, `ENABLED_NO_ROOT` after `rmdir`, `ENABLED_OK` for a valid dir, `M12_SYNC_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` from `RunIfEnabled` when the root is unusable, `ApplyConfig(NULL)` disables, `ApplyConfig` round-trips the flag + dir + policy, a re-disabled flag reverts the boundary at the next check, and `DiscoverSaveFiles` adds 2/2 `*.sav` entries, ignores `*.txt`, and is idempotent. Verification: `cmake --build build --target firestaff_m12_cloud_sync_probe --parallel` clean, `gcc -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wno-format-truncation -Iinclude -Isrc -c probes/m12/firestaff_m12_cloud_sync_probe.c` clean, direct probe PASS 38/38, focused CTest `m12_cloud_sync_boundary` PASS 1/1, broader `m12_*` regression set PASS 11/12 with the single failure (`m12_polished_ui_flow`) confirmed pre-existing on `origin/main` via `git stash`, full project `cmake --build build` PASS, `git diff --check` clean. Honest scope: launcher/settings + runtime boundary only — directory-based sync model, no real cloud provider, no `m12_save_browser_export_import` payload movement, no README claim, and no promotion of the `Cloud sync` row in `docs/FIRESTAFF_GAP_LIST.md` from `OPEN-LARGE` (real cloud provider integration, multi-device encryption, conflict resolution UI, and push/pull scheduling remain open).

- ✅ 2026-06-28 runtime gesture navigation gate (input translation + touch target safety): added `runtime_gesture_navigation_gate` module (`include/runtime_gesture_navigation_gate.h` + `src/engine/runtime_gesture_navigation_gate.c`) plus data-free CTest unit `tests/test_runtime_gesture_navigation_gate.c` (15 invariant groups, 50+ PASS) and headless CI probe `probes/m11/firestaff_runtime_gesture_navigation_gate_probe.c` (9 groups + 50-iteration determinism, status=PASS). The gate is the deterministic cross-game contract behind the existing `firestaff_touch.c` swipe + edge-strafe primitives: `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNav_Evaluate(event, policy, result)` consumes a `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNavEvent` (framebuffer-space start/end coords + threshold/tolerance) and a `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNavPolicy` (`accessibilityTouchEnabled`, `v2PresentationEnabled`, `v1ParityPreserve`) and returns a `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNavDecision` + `FS_Command` code mapped to the existing `FS_CMD_*` enum (`FS_CMD_MOVE_FORWARD=1 / _MOVE_BACKWARD=2 / _TURN_LEFT=3 / _TURN_RIGHT=4 / _STRAFE_LEFT=5 / _STRAFE_RIGHT=6`) so callers can index a single integer. Swipe up/down/left/right map to move_forward / move_backward / turn_left / turn_right (cross-V1/V2 path - the same FS_Command codes the V1 keyboard path already consumes via `fs_input_queue_push`); edge-left/right map to strafe_left / strafe_right and are V2-only with `v1ParityPreserve` + `v2PresentationEnabled` guard. The gate rejects six boundary cases: `rejected_disabled` (touch setting off), `rejected_too_short` (travel below `FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_SWIPE_THRESHOLD_PX=40` or below the caller's `tapTolerancePx<=FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_TAP_TOLERANCE_PX=24` tap-tolerance guard), `rejected_too_small_target` (edge zone narrower than the 44 px Apple HIG / WCAG 2.5.5 floor pinned by `RUNTIME_GESTURE_NAV_MIN_TARGET_PX`), `rejected_ambiguous` (diagonal swipe with equal horizontal/vertical axis), `rejected_null` (NULL event/policy safety), and `rejected_v1_only` (V2 edge-strafe called when `v2PresentationEnabled=0` or `v1ParityPreserve=1`). `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNav_TouchTargetSafe(w, h)` is the touch-target safety contract (returns 1 when both axes >= 44 px, 0 when either is negative or below floor) and `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNav_SourceViewportSafe(sourceW, sourceH, surfaceW, surfaceH)` extends the floor to source-viewport scale safety (the 320x200 source framebuffer's shortest axis must scale to >= 44 px on the running surface). Source-locked against ReDMCSB `COMMAND.C:2045-2155 F0380_COMMAND_ProcessQueue_CPSC` (movement/turn queue dispatch that consumes the same C001..C006 movement IDs), `CLIKMENU.C:142-174 F0365 turn` (turn dispatch), `CLIKMENU.C:180-390 F0366 move` (step dispatch), `GAMELOOP.C:164-219 V1 input wait loop` (V1 parity surface), `DEFS.H:238-243 C001..C006 movement commands`, `DEFS.H:197-211 C003/C005 strafe owner`, `src/engine/firestaff_touch.c FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_SWIPE_THRESHOLD_PX=40 / FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_TAP_TOLERANCE_PX=24 / FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_LONG_PRESS_MS=500 / FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_EDGE_ZONE_FRAC=0.20`, `src/dm1v2/dm1_v2_touch_controller_affordance_pc34.c DM1_V2_AFFORDANCE_TOUCH_EDGE_STRAFE_LEFT/RIGHT` (V2-only edge-strafe affordance enumeration), and `include/config_m12.h dm1V2AccessibilityTouchEnabled` (the launcher setting that gates the whole contract). - ✅ 2026-06-26 X68000 HDM real-media receipt + cross-module FTL-handoff gates: added `probes/x68k/firestaff_x68k_media_receipt_real_corpus_probe.c` (skip-safe CTest `firestaff_x68k_media_receipt_real_corpus`, 10/10 PASS) and `probes/x68k/firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff_real_corpus_probe.c` (skip-safe CTest `firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff_real_corpus`, 8/8 PASS) on top of the existing data-free `firestaff_x68k_media_classify_unit` (12/12) and synthetic-FTL `firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff_unit` (5/5). The new receipt probe verifies the DMWeb-documented 2DHD X68000 geometry and protection-sector surface against the local public DMFiles DM1 X68000 v3.0 HDM `~/.firestaff/data/dm1-extras/x68000-3.0-jp/DungeonMasterX68000version30Japanese.hdm` (1,261,568 bytes, exact DMWeb `2 sides * 77 tracks * 8 sectors * 1024 bytes`): full-disk class, no FTL 0x6160 magic at offset 0, Hudson Soft boot block at offset 0 (`60 1c ...`), 1024/1024 `0xE5E5...` MFM-fill bytes in the DMWeb-documented Track 1 Side 1 Sector 9 region (the documented public-DMFiles state, which lacks the protection sector), no `HPR-0007` sentinel at the DMWeb-documented sector-9 linear offset (so a future re-issued master that puts one there will flip this receipt to FAIL with a clear diff), `IsUnprotectedDisk == 0` because the protection region is MFM fill not zero, and `IsFTLPayload == 0` because the HDM starts with the Hudson Soft boot block. The new handoff probe scans the same real HDM for embedded FTL resources via `FirestaffFtlContainer_Parse` (greatstone `d_ftl.html` common-header magic 0x6160 big-endian, hunk_count at offset 18) and finds **2 parseable FTL containers** at offsets 73,728 (0x12000) and 460,800 (0x70800); the first FTL's BSS `data_area1_memory_size` (24,720 bytes) is verified to fit the on-disk HDM media class via `FirestaffX68kMedia_FTLHandoffFits`, and the helper's documented boundary cases are cross-checked on the real media (`size+1` reject, `0` accept as size-unknown, `disk_bytes` accept). Source of truth: dmweb-free.fr/community/documentation/copy-protection "Sharp X68000" section (2DHD geometry, `HPR-0007` sentinel, MFM no-flux-area), dmweb DM X68000 edition page (HDM original image that cannot boot without protection sectors), greatstone `d_ftl.html` "20-byte common header" magic 0x6160 BE and Note 7 handoff math, the existing `include/firestaff_x68k_media_classify.h` (constants, scan flags, FTLHandoffFits) and `include/firestaff_ftl_container.h` (parser contract). **Known limitation surfaced:** the classifier's `ftl_magic_candidate_count` field scans only the first 32 KiB (per its documented contract for single-resource `.FTL` payloads) but the real DMFiles X68000 HDM embeds FTL resources at offsets > 32 KiB, so the candidate-count field reads 0 even though the full-HDM scan finds 2 parseable FTL containers. The receipt explicitly surfaces both numbers as notes (`classifier ftl_magic_candidate_count (first 32 KiB) = 0; full-HDM parseable FTL count = 2`) rather than asserting a false-positive guarantee. Disjoint from the data-free `firestaff_x68k_media_classify_unit` (which stays data-free so CI runs without real media) and the synthetic-FTL `firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff_unit` (which validates the handoff math against an in-memory synthetic FTL container). Skip-safe: hosts without a known DM1 X68000 HDM exit 0 with a SKIP message on both probes. The probes do NOT vend game data, do NOT parse MFM flux timing, do NOT claim original-vs-cracked-vs-save-disk authenticity (the off-axis `HPR-0007` strings embedded in `B:\\DMGame.bak` backup labels are surfaced as a separate finding for the TODO follow-up), do NOT provide 31 kHz presentation evidence, and do NOT cover X68000 keypad/arrow input gates or emulator/runtime launch proof — those remain tracked in `docs/FIRESTAFF_GAP_LIST.md` and the `TODO.md` 2026-06-25 row. Verification: `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DBUILD_TESTING=ON`, `cmake --build build --target firestaff_x68k_media_receipt_real_corpus_probe firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff_real_corpus_probe test_firestaff_x68k_media_classify test_firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff --parallel 4` clean (no warnings under `-Wall -Wextra -pedantic -O2`), strict CI `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wno-format-truncation -std=c99` clean on both new probe sources, `ctest --test-dir build -R '^firestaff_x68k_' --output-on-failure` PASS 4/4 (data-free classifier + synthetic-FTL handoff + real-media receipt + real-media FTL handoff), focused regression set `ctest -R '^(firestaff_x68k_|firestaff_ftl_container_unit|firestaff_ftl_hunk_data_zero_run_unit)'` PASS 6/6, `tools/asset-validate/no_game_data_in_git.py` PASS, `git diff --check HEAD` clean. Default probe path: `~/.firestaff/data/dm1-extras/x68000-3.0-jp/DungeonMasterX68000version30Japanese.hdm` (operator can override via `FIRESTAFF_X68K_HDM_PATH=<path>`); the DMFiles English DIM is intentionally not in the default candidate list (256-byte DIM header changes the on-disk byte alignment and would fail the size receipt honestly).

- ✅ 2026-06-26 CSB Hint Oracle UI/runtime binding gate: added `csb_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding` (include + src/csb) on top of the existing `csb_hint_oracle_htc` format-contract parser and the `csb_hint_oracle_htc_real_scan` real-asset scan/cache. The new module exposes three runtime-adjacent binding surfaces that prove a decoded HCSB.HTC page or page-slice can reach a Firestaff-facing oracle/hint surface (a printable text/buffer the launcher or M11 view can render): `csb_hint_oracle_ui_binding_format_report()` writes a multi-line diagnostic/oracle report (matched MD5 + label, file size, resolved path, format word + dungeon id, location/hint/page counts, the hint 0 first-page binding smoke, and the level=0 (255, 255) wildcard binding smoke); `csb_hint_oracle_ui_binding_format_hint(hint_index)` writes the hint name + first-page decoded text for any hint; `csb_hint_oracle_ui_binding_resolve_location(level, x, y)` resolves a (level, x, y) into the first matching hint's name + first-page decoded text. Source-locked: ReDMCSB `HINTLOAD.C:11-18`, `HINTHTC.C:177-358`, `HINTLZW.C:122-212`, plus dmweb Hint Oracle Files page. The binding surface is intentionally small: it does not draw a graphical Hint Oracle overlay, it does not bind into the M11 game loop or M12 launch flow, and it does not claim parity for every Utility Disk release variant — the known-hash list in `csb_hint_oracle_htc_real_scan` still gates which HCSB.HTCs we accept; the binding surface itself is variant-agnostic. CTest-gated as `csb_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding_unit` (data-free, synthetic in-memory fixture, 6/6 invariants PASS: not-loaded argument handling, report contains the binding smoke (matched MD5/label + format word + dungeon id + counts + hint 0 first-page text "Cast/ZOKATHRA" + wildcard resolve surface), format_hint round-trip, resolve_location binding (level=5 (255,255) → hint 1 "ANYWHERE" + first-page text "Anywhere"), truncation path, result-name table) and `csb_v1_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding` (real-asset, `firestaff_csb_v1_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding_probe.c`, labels `tier2;csb;hint_oracle;real_data;skip_safe`, 32/32 invariants PASS). End-to-end on the local Atari ST 2.x HCSB.HTC (md5 `8ce69b54cf255a15e98e909bb45b9742`, 66,172 bytes): binding report surfaces the matched MD5/label + format word 2 + dungeon id 13 + the parsed location/hint/page counts; `format_hint(0)` writes the hint 0 "FULYA PIT" header + the parsed first-page text starting `"This is where Lord Chaos mined the deadly Mana-absorbing Corbum.."` (printable ASCII, full text round-trips); `resolve_location(level=0, 255, 255)` resolves to hint 197 "CREATURES" and writes the first-page text starting `"Learn well the shapes and forms dread Chaos make"` (the binding surface reaches a real decoded HCSB.HTC page on the verified Utility Disk HCSB.HTC); second scan + binding is byte-identical to the first (deterministic); out-of-range hint index and non-matching (level, x, y) tuples return the documented error codes with empty buffers; `(not loaded)` is written when the cache is empty. Disjoint from `csb_hint_oracle_htc_unit` (data-free parser) and from `csb_v1_hint_oracle_real_htc_scan` (scan/cache); the binding surface reuses both. Verification: `cmake --build build --target firestaff_csb_v1_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding_probe test_csb_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding`, `ctest --test-dir build -R '^hint_oracle' --output-on-failure` PASS 4/4 (data-free parser + data-free binding + real-asset scan + real-asset binding), strict `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic` clean on probe + test + binding source, `tools/asset-validate/no_game_data_in_git.py` PASS, `git diff --check HEAD` clean. Skip-safe: hosts without a known HCSB.HTC exit 0 with a SKIP message on the real-asset probe. The actual Hint Oracle graphical overlay, parsing additional Utility Disk release variants (English R1/R2/R3, French R1, German R1/R2), and real page/screen verification against a verified HCSB.HTC remain tracked in `docs/FIRESTAFF_GAP_LIST.md` row "HTC hint oracle text format (CSB)" and the `TODO.md` 2026-06-25 follow-up row.

- ✅ 2026-06-25 Nexus V1 Saturn-font SEGA SATURN SCR section-table parser + helpers: added `nexus_v1_font_load_sections()` (plus `nexus_v1_font_section_count` / `_get_section` / `_section_table_index` / `_section_in_bounds`) to `src/nexus/nexus_v1_saturn_font.c` (existing flat 1bpp `nexus_v1_font_load()` remains the runtime path) and the corresponding `Nexus_V1_FontSections` / `Nexus_V1_FontSection` types + section-table constants in `include/nexus_v1_saturn_font.h`. Walks the 32-entry SEGA SATURN SCR section table at offset 0x20, treats (offset=0, size=0) as reserved/empty, skips entries whose (offset, size) window fails bounds checks or overlaps the section table itself, preserves the original table index across skips, and stays bounded by reporting only well-formed sections. Source-locked against the SEGA SATURN SCR format (16-byte "SEGA SATURN SCR\0" magic + 16-byte descriptor block at 0x10/0x14 + 256-byte table at 0x20) and the verified local FONT256.S2D (25,012 bytes). New headless probe `firestaff_nexus_v1_saturn_font_scr_sections_probe` (ctest `nexus_v1_saturn_font_scr_sections`, 55/55 PASS) covers NULL-safety, too-small-buffer rejection, invalid-magic rejection, all-reserved/zero entry skipping, single-populated-entry handling, out-of-bounds section skipping, table-overlap skipping, four-populated FONT256.S2D-shape layout (indices 0/2/4/6), in-bounds validation, original-index preservation across skips, and a fully-bound four-populated real-asset chain (entries 0x0120+0x2010 / 0x2130+0x3c90 / 0x5dc0+0x0210 / 0x5fd0+0x01e4 form a contiguous non-overlapping partition that ends at 0x61b4 inside the verified 25,012-byte asset; entries 28..31 with non-zero but out-of-bounds values are skipped without rejecting the whole table). Verification: `cmake --build build --target firestaff_nexus_v1_saturn_font_scr_sections_probe`, `ctest --test-dir build -R '^nexus_v1_saturn_font_scr_sections$' --output-on-failure` PASS, plus the existing `nexus_v1_saturn_font_determinism` (16/16) and `nexus_v1_saturn_font_render` (32/32) still PASS unchanged, and `git diff --check` clean. - ✅ 2026-06-28 Nexus V1 S2D runtime text-layout binding + screen-text probe: new `nexus_v1_s2d_text_layout` module (`include/nexus_v1_s2d_text_layout.h`, `src/nexus/nexus_v1_s2d_text_layout.c`) binds the existing SCR section-table parser + flat 1bpp renderer to a minimal runtime text-layout cursor. `nexus_v1_s2d_section_glyph_map()` walks the parsed `Nexus_V1_FontSections` and produces a bounded `Nexus_V1_S2D_SectionGlyphMap` that maps each populated section to its `(char_start, char_count)` slice of the character table, capped against `bytes_per_glyph` and the SCR header `char_count`. `nexus_v1_s2d_glyph_range_lookup()` routes a glyph index to the matching range; `nexus_v1_s2d_glyph_map_total_chars()` sums the populated ranges. `Nexus_V1_S2D_TextLayout` owns a borrowed pointer to the font + map + config and a `Nexus_V1_S2D_TextCursor` (cursor_x/y, line_count, chars_drawn/skipped/clipped, writes, max_chars cap). `nexus_v1_s2d_text_layout_draw_string()` walks an ASCII string, dispatches each glyph through the existing `nexus_v1_font_draw_glyph_indexed()` per the looked-up section, advances the cursor by `char_width + letter_spacing_x`, breaks on `'\n'`, and steps on `'\t'`; non-printable bytes are skipped. `nexus_v1_s2d_text_layout_free()` and `_reset_cursor()` round out the lifecycle; the macOS secure-memset trap (`memset(&layout, 0, ...)` where `&layout` is a pointer-to-pointer and `__darwin_obsz0` sees the wrong size) is documented and avoided. New CTest-gated headless probe `firestaff_nexus_v1_s2d_runtime_text_layout_probe` (ctest `nexus_v1_s2d_runtime_text_layout`, 99/99 PASS) covers: NULL-safety on every entry point; bytes_per_glyph=0 rejection; empty/single/four-populated synthetic SCR map invariants (range_count, char_start forms a contiguous partition, total_chars, original table index preserved across skips, header cap honored); out-of-coverage `glyph_range_lookup` returns -1; layout init NULL-safety; reset_cursor clears counters; `draw_string("")` returns 0 and does not modify the framebuffer hash; single-glyph draw + cursor advance by `char_width + letter_spacing_x`; 5-glyph cursor lands at `5*(char_width + letter_spacing_x)`; `'\n'` increments `line_count`/`newline_count`, resets `cursor_x`, advances `cursor_y` by `line_height`; deterministic FNV-1a framebuffer hash across two runs of `"NEXUS"`; `max_chars` cap stops drawing at the cap; out-of-coverage chars increment `chars_skipped`; real-asset `FONT256.S2D` skip-safe path (when `~/.firestaff/data/nexus/FONT256.S2D` is staged) loads the verified 25,012-byte asset, builds a section→glyph-range map that covers all 256 chars through table index 0 (section [0] = 0x2010 bytes / 32 = 256 chars), runs the layout over `"NEXUS"` 3 times, and asserts the FNV-1a framebuffer hash is bit-identical across all three runs. Source-lock: `include/nexus_v1_saturn_font.h` (existing section-table constants), `src/nexus/nexus_v1_saturn_font.c` (`nexus_v1_font_draw_glyph_indexed`, `nexus_v1_font_load_sections`), SEGA SATURN SCR format (16-byte magic + 16-byte descriptor + 256-byte section table), the verified `FONT256.S2D` 4-section layout, and the ReDMCSB DM1 `DUNVIEW.C:3679-3706` fixed-width advance convention. Verification: `cmake --build build --target firestaff_nexus_v1_s2d_runtime_text_layout_probe` clean under `-Wall -Wextra -O2`; focused CTest `nexus_v1_saturn_font_determinism|nexus_v1_saturn_font_render|nexus_v1_saturn_font_scr_sections|nexus_v1_s2d_runtime_text_layout` PASS 4/4; the full `ctest --test-dir build -R nexus` PASS 45/45; `git diff --check` clean. Stays bounded: ASCII-only printable subset (no Shift-JIS double-byte decode), no real Nexus screen capture, no original-vs-Firestaff pixel diff — those remain separate gaps in `docs/FIRESTAFF_GAP_LIST.md`.

Real-asset/runtime regression for one narrow DM1 V1 Hall of Champions champion-portrait slice: ordinal 22 (C026 column 6 row 2, the GOTHMOG slot of the 8x3 atlas), route variant `d2c_far_positive` (party stands at (1,3) facing NORTH on Hall map 0 — the D1C cell (1,2) has no C127 sensor, so the D1C front-mirror ordinal helper reports -1 and the D1C portrait is NOT drawn at this view distance; the D2C cell (1,1) carries the C127 sensor with sensorData=1 HALK, observable by the F0128 D2C dispatch at DUNVIEW.C:8520-8521 — hence "D2C far positive"), aspect `portrait_rect_position` (D1C front-wall portrait cutout at viewport (96,35) sized 32x29). The probe locks six invariants against the live C026 GRAPHICS.DAT portrait strip and real DM1 V1 PC 3.4 DUNGEON.DAT. (A) C026 atlas math for ordinal 22: col=22&7=6, row=22>>3=2, source rect (192, 58, 32, 29) inside the 256x87 atlas with row-2 source bottom exactly reaching the atlas height (87), plus the all-24-ordinals in-strip check. (B) Catalog identity: `M11_GameView_GetMirrorNameByOrdinal(22) == "GOTHMOG"` and the title slot is empty (untitled champion). (C) D2C-far route pose at (1,3,N): D1C front-mirror ordinal == -1 (the (1,2) cell has no C127 sensor) and at least one C127 sensor exists in `things[]` (the F0128 D2C dispatch is well-formed). (D) D1C wall-ornament frame helper returns the source-locked (80, 29, 64, 43) box at both the D2C-far pose (1,3,N) and the D1C-near pose (1,2,N) — the frame geometry is depth-invariant, and the (96, 35) D1C cutout sits inside the wall frame with depth-invariant offset (16, 39). (E) D2C-far route seed via C127 sensor rewrite at the (1,1) D2C cell from sensorData=1 to sensorData=22: the D2C-far pose (1,3,N) still reports -1 on the D1C depth (D1C portrait not drawn at D2C-far view), but walking forward one cell to (1,2,N) reveals ordinal 22 at the D1C depth (D2C->D1C transition) — this is the core "d2c_far_positive" contract: the F0128 D2C dispatch has a real ordinal at the D2C cell, and that ordinal becomes the D1C portrait_rect when the party closes the D1C view distance. The sensor is restored before the probe exits. (F) No-floating contract for D2C-far D2L2/D2R2 side walls: the D2L2/D2R2 view geometry (cells (0,3), (2,3), (0,2), (2,2), (1,3,W)) and the (1,2) EAST/WEST side walls do NOT expose ordinal 22 after the route seed — the portrait sprite is bound to the (1,1) D2C cell, not to the side lanes. Source-locked against ReDMCSB DUNGEON.C:2558,2573,2608-2612 (C127 sensorData → G0289, M011_CELL(sensor) → visible wall cell), MOVESENS.C:1501-1503 (C127 → F0280), REVIVE.C F0280,F0282 (candidate materialise/disable), DUNVIEW.C:3913-3928 (C346 frame + C026 portrait blit at D1C), DUNVIEW.C:8318-8542 F0128 (far-to-near draw order), DUNVIEW.C:8520-8521 F0128 (D2C dispatch before D1C), COORD.C:1693-1722 (PC 3.4 viewport origin / 224x136 dimensions), DEFS.H:821-826 (M027/M028 portrait X/Y macros), DEFS.H:2071-2079 (G2071_C320/G2078_C32/G2079_C29 zone constants). Verification: focused build clean with `-Wall -Wextra -O2` (only the harmless `ld: warning: ignoring duplicate libraries` warning from the existing foreach block), focused direct probe PASS 38/38 against local DM1 V1 PC 3.4 DUNGEON.DAT (C026 atlas math 10/10, catalog identity 4/4, D2C-far route pose 2/2, D1C wall-ornament zone contract 12/12, D2C-far route seed 8/8, no-floating side-lane contract 5/5), `ctest --test-dir build -R '^firestaff_dm1_v1_hall_champion_portrait_22_d2c_far_positive_runtime_probe$'` PASS 1/1 in 93.87s, and `git diff --check` clean. Companion slice to `firestaff_dm1_v1_hall_champion_portrait_22_front_north_entry_runtime_probe` (depth-1 D1C view) and `firestaff_dm1_v1_hall_of_champions_portrait_22_redraw_after_candidate_runtime_probe` (redraw after candidate panel) — they share the same catalog / atlas math source-locks; the new assertion is the D2C-far positive (depth-2) view contract. - ✅ 2026-06-22 ISO 9660 / BIN scanner case-insensitive + duplicate-hash tiebreak: extended `src/shared/asset_find_by_hash.c` so `scan_iso_dir_by_md5` and `scan_iso_dir_by_md5_list` walk the entire ISO root directory before returning and pick the case-insensitively-smallest entry name per matching MD5 (mirrors the existing ZIP `is_better_zip_entry` tiebreak in `scan_zip_by_md5`). New helper `is_better_iso_entry` uses `asset_casecmp` per ISO 9660:1988 §7.5 (file identifiers compare case-insensitively at the filesystem level, even though on-disk bytes may preserve Joliet/lower-case form). New data-free CTest `asset_find_by_hash_iso_case_duplicate` builds synthetic PVD + root-directory fixtures with hand-rolled ISO 9660 directory records and pins both regressions: (a) Joliet-like mixed-case entries ("dungeon.dat" alongside "DUNGEON.DAT") report the on-disk lowercase name in the virtual path, including round-trip extraction and uppercase-hex MD5 normalization; (b) duplicate-hash entries ("Z_DUPLICATE.DAT" first, then "A_DUPLICATE.DAT") deterministically report the lexicographically smaller entry. Verification: `ctest --test-dir build -R '^asset_find_by_hash(_iso_case_duplicate)?$' --output-on-failure` PASS 2/2 and the broader Tier 1 strict boot probe still passes across all five games (`tier1_strict_boot_probe` PASS). Source-locked against ISO 9660:1988 §6.8.1 (Directory Record), ISO 9660:1988 §7.5 (case-insensitive file identification), and ReDMCSB CEDTINCA.C F7059_ReadDungeonPartWithChecksum (hash-verified asset identity contract). This is scanner determinism / virtual-path-reporting regression coverage only; no gameplay, no real-asset launch, no broader ISO/Joliet extension work.
- ✅ 2026-06-22 Nested deflated ZIP entry → asset-cache materialization regression: added `tests/test_asset_status_zip_cache_nested_deflate.c` and registered it as CTest target `asset_status_zip_cache_nested_deflate`. The fixture synthesizes a single ZIP whose graphics entry sits at the deeply-nested path `nested/inner/level1/level2/DM2GRAPHICS.DAT` and whose dungeon entry is flat; both are deflated (method=8) when zlib is available so the deflate stream is strictly smaller than the source payload (the inflate code path is what is actually exercised, not a stored-entry fallback). The gate proves three layers end-to-end: (1) the recursive hash scanner reports the match as a virtual path `<zip>::<nested/.../ENTRY>` and preserves every path segment of the nested entry name; (2) the low-level `asset_extract_virtual_path()` helper inflates the deflate stream and writes a byte-identical ordinary file; (3) the M12 cache materializer rewrites both required-file matched paths to ordinary files under `<userDataDir>/asset-cache/dm2/{GRAPHICS,DUNGEON}.DAT` so the runtime never has to understand virtual container paths. CMake `pkg_check_modules(ZLIB)` now drives `FIRESTAFF_HAS_ZLIB` (default OFF) so the test gets `FIRESTAFF_HAS_ZLIB=1` plus `PkgConfig::ZLIB` on hosts with zlib, and falls back to stored entries otherwise. Verification: `cmake --build build --target test_asset_status_zip_cache_nested_deflate` clean with `-Wall -Wextra -O2`, focused CTest PASS, and `asset_find_by_hash` / `dm1_pc34_multilanguage_required_gate` / asset-cache CTests all still PASS. Source-locked against `src/shared/asset_find_by_hash.c` (zip_stored_entry_md5 / zip_deflated_entry_md5 / scan_zip_by_md5 / zip_deflated_entry_extract / asset_extract_virtual_path) and `src/shared/asset_status_m12.c` (m12_path_is_virtual_asset / m12_materialize_required_file / m12_materialize_runtime_cache_for_game). This is a cache-handoff contract regression only; it does not claim original capture parity, real CSB/DM2 launch paths, or pixel evidence.

- ✅ 2026-06-22 Nested deflated ZIP entry → asset-cache materialization regression: added `tests/test_asset_status_zip_cache_nested_deflate.c` and registered it as CTest target `asset_status_zip_cache_nested_deflate`. The fixture synthesizes a single ZIP whose graphics entry sits at the deeply-nested path `nested/inner/level1/level2/DM2GRAPHICS.DAT` and whose dungeon entry is flat; both are deflated (method=8) when zlib is available so the deflate stream is strictly smaller than the source payload (the inflate code path is what is actually exercised, not a stored-entry fallback). The gate proves three layers end-to-end: (1) the recursive hash scanner reports the match as a virtual path `<zip>::<nested/.../ENTRY>` and preserves every path segment of the nested entry name; (2) the low-level `asset_extract_virtual_path()` helper inflates the deflate stream and writes a byte-identical ordinary file; (3) the M12 cache materializer rewrites both required-file matched paths to ordinary files under `<userDataDir>/asset-cache/dm2/{GRAPHICS,DUNGEON}.DAT` so the runtime never has to understand virtual container paths. CMake `pkg_check_modules(ZLIB)` now drives `FIRESTAFF_HAS_ZLIB` (default OFF) so the test gets `FIRESTAFF_HAS_ZLIB=1` plus `PkgConfig::ZLIB` on hosts with zlib, and falls back to stored entries otherwise. Verification: `cmake --build build --target test_asset_status_zip_cache_nested_deflate` clean with `-Wall -Wextra -O2`, focused CTest PASS, and `asset_find_by_hash` / `dm1_pc34_multilanguage_required_gate` / asset-cache CTests all still PASS. Source-locked against `src/shared/asset_find_by_hash.c` (zip_stored_entry_md5 / zip_deflated_entry_md5 / scan_zip_by_md5 / zip_deflated_entry_extract / asset_extract_virtual_path) and `src/shared/asset_status_m12.c` (m12_path_is_virtual_asset / m12_materialize_required_file / m12_materialize_runtime_cache_for_game). This is a cache-handoff contract regression only; it does not claim original capture parity, real CSB/DM2 launch paths, or pixel evidence.

- ✅ 2026-06-28 Launcher session timer runtime overlay: landed the in-game handoff boundary for the launcher-owned Session Timer setting (`Off` / `15m` / `30m` / `60m` / `120m`) so the M11 game view now consults the persisted limit during gameplay and surfaces a deterministic reminder overlay + forced-pause confirm dialog instead of silently running past the user's chosen cap. New module `src/shared/session_timer_runtime.c` + header `include/session_timer_runtime.h` owns the runtime state machine: `SessionTimerRuntime_Init(limitMinutes)` seeds the limit, `SessionTimerRuntime_Tick(seconds)` accumulates elapsed seconds, `SessionTimerRuntime_Poll()` reports one of three events (`SESSION_TIMER_RUNTIME_EVENT_RUNNING`, `_EVENT_REMINDER_DUE`, `_EVENT_FORCED_PAUSE`), `SessionTimerRuntime_Acknowledge()` clears the pending reminder latch + re-arms the next window, `SessionTimerRuntime_ClearForcedPause()` releases the latch, and `SessionTimerRuntime_FormatRemaining(buf, size)` writes `HH:MM:SS` / `Off`. The reminder threshold + re-arm window default to 300 s (5 min) and are documented constants, not ReDMCSB-derived. Off-mode + negative ticks + post-limit ticks + null-pointer inputs are all safe no-ops; pre-arm at init when `limitSeconds <= reminderThresholdSeconds` so a 1-min limit surfaces the reminder up front. M11 wire-up: `include/m11_game_view.h` adds `sessionTimerRuntime` + `sessionTimerForcedPauseDialogActive` + `sessionTimerReminderOverlayActive` fields, and the `M11_GameView_InitFromMenuSessionTimer / Tick / Acknowledge / ClearForcedPause / GetForcedPauseDialogActive / GetReminderOverlayActive` API; `M11_GameView_OpenSelectedMenuEntry` (src/engine/m11_game_view.c:7169-7170) seeds the runtime from `M12_StartupMenu_SessionTimerLimitMinutes(menuState)` at every game launch and the CSB/Theron V2 settings bridge keeps its existing branch; `M11_GameView_Draw` (src/engine/m11_game_view.c:~28310) paints the reminder banner (200x14 yellow-on-black top strip with `SESSION TIMER HH:MM:SS REMAINING`) and the forced-pause confirm dialog (240x60 dimmed-centered box with `SESSION TIMER EXPIRED (HH:MM:SS) -- RETURN TO MENU` + `PRESS ENTER TO RETURN TO MENU` / `ESC TO DISMISS`); `M11_GameView_HandleInput` (src/engine/m11_game_view.c:~8430) gates ACCEPT/ACTION on the forced-pause dialog to return-to-launcher and BACK to dismiss-and-resume, and any non-NONE input dismisses the reminder banner; `M11_GameView_Shutdown` / `_Init` keep the same memset-zero contract so the runtime is freshly seeded at every launch (no leftover FORCED_PAUSE latch from a previous run). The main loop in `src/engine/main_loop_m11.c:2720-2735` ticks the runtime once per >=1 s of active gameplay via `M11_GameView_TickSessionTimer(&gameView, loopDeltaMs/1000)` and lets the runtime's Off-mode + post-limit no-op semantics keep the loop safe even when the user has the timer set to Off. The runtime is a Firestaff UX boundary — there is no original DM1/CSB/DM2/Nexus/Theron title-screen timer on PC 3.4 to source-lock against, and no ReDMCSB line numbers are cited because no gameplay behavior is touched. Verification: new CTest target `session_timer_runtime` (tests/test_session_timer_runtime.c, all-PASS) covers Off-mode, 60-min boundary math, REMINDER_DUE latch + Acknowledge re-arm, FORCED_PAUSE latch + ClearForcedPause, post-clear re-latch on a 1s tick, Reset preserves limit, FormatRemaining for Off/HH:MM:SS/null/zero-buffer, default-exposure sanity, null-pointer tolerance, and the 1-min limit immediate reminder pre-arm; new CTest target `session_timer_runtime_probe` (probes/runtime/firestaff_session_timer_runtime_probe.c, all-PASS 12/12) covers the M11/M12 hand-off smoke (launcher Off-mode -> runtime Off-mode, 60-min runtime surfaces REMINDER_DUE at the 55-min boundary with the documented 300 s threshold, Acknowledge + 60 s tick stays in RUNNING within the re-arm window, 60-min runtime surfaces FORCED_PAUSE at the limit, FormatRemaining matches `M12_StartupMenu_SessionTimerRemainingSeconds`, `M12_CampaignSessionTimer` flushes into slot independent of runtime state, ClearForcedPause + zero-tick leaves runtime in RUNNING, 15-min limit reports RUNNING while 1-min limit reports REMINDER_DUE at init, Reset returns to RUNNING with full limit, launcher round-trip across 0/15/30/60/120 minutes stays coherent, default reminder + re-arm window = 300 s); the existing `m12_session_timer`, `campaign_m12_session_timer`, `m12_startup_menu`, `m12_menu_mouse`, `m12_language_cycle_layout`, `m11_phase_a`, `m11_high_contrast_overlay_pc34_compat`, `m11_high_contrast_overlay_runtime_probe`, `m12_launcher_screen_reader_manifest`, and `firestaff_accessibility_manifest_unit` all still PASS; `git diff --check` clean; `-Wall -Wextra -O2` clean on every new + touched file. `TODO.md` / `docs/FIRESTAFF_GAP_LIST.md` Session Timer row can move from `OPEN-BOUNDED` to `FIXED` (launcher settings + campaign playtime + in-game reminder/forced-pause overlay all in place); remaining work is the original-capture/screenshot evidence that the overlay actually paints against real assets, which lives outside this handoff boundary.

Per-anchor id words observed locally in the hash-verified raw BINs: US anchor 0 = `0x01725800` at `0x2d53dc`, anchor 1 = `0x01600801` at `0x47d03c`, anchor 2 = `0x01122401` at `0x71283c`; JP anchor 0 = `0x01530301` at `0x2d4aac`, anchor 1 = `0x01411301` at `0x47c70c`, anchor 2 = `0x01682801` at `0x711f0c`. `Theron_Track02BankSignal` extended with `audio_bank_id[3]`, `audio_bank_id_offsets[3]`, `audio_bank_prefix_offsets[3]`, `audio_bank_id_recognized[3]` and is populated by `find_raw_bin_bank_signal()` alongside the existing descriptor/span data. The one-shot helper is hash-gated to raw BIN variants; US Track 02 ISO (partial extract, no anchor) and JP Rev 1 ISO (zero-filled image) return `THERON_TRACK02_SIGNAL_UNSUPPORTED_VARIANT` rather than `NOT_FOUND`. `firestaff_theron_v1_track02_bank_probe` adds a synthetic-positive fixture at the real JP anchor 0 offset (id `0x12345678`), a missing-prefix negative fixture, an out-of-range anchor-index negative fixture, a NULL-input fixture, an unsupported-variant fixture for US ISO + JP Rev 1 ISO + unknown MD5, and an opt-in real-data fixture that locks US anchor 0 id `0x01725800` at offset `0x2d53dc` and JP anchor 0 id `0x01530301` at offset `0x2d4aac` (skipped when the raw BIN paths are absent). All 30 Theron-related CTest gates stay green. Source/evidence: `src/theron/theron_v1_track02.c` post-boundary span fingerprinting; `docs/source-lock/tqr_v1_phase2_data_formats_H2339.md §10.2` (ADPCM data block location is STUB; this marker is one ADPCM-bank anchor candidate). - ✅ 2026-06-22 Theron V1 save/load progress round-trip regression: new `test_theron_v1_save_progress_roundtrip_pc34` data-free CTest target packs a real Theron_V1_Party (Theron + Mara + Vey + Ruk, mid-Crypt-of-Shadows, item reset applied, gold 4321, second quest item set) through `theron_v1_party_pack` into the slot champion stream, writes slot 4 via `theron_v1_save_to_slot`, reads it back via `theron_v1_save_load_from_slot`, and unpacks via `theron_v1_party_unpack`. Every documented `Theron_V1_Champion` field (name, health/max, mana/max, stamina/max, stats, skill levels, wounds, alive flag, primary_class, portrait_index, inventory slots, equipment slots, food/water) is asserted byte-equal across the round-trip plus the parallel `Theron_DungeonProgression` invariants (current_dungeon/level, dungeon_states, quest_items_collected/in_current_dungeon, item_reset_mode/applied, dungeon_playtime_seconds, seeds). A re-save overwrite round-trip locks slot-hygiene (no stale-tail/partial-write). The regression test caught a real bug: `theron_v1_save_load_from_slot` returned `Theron_SaveSlot.slot_index = 0` regardless of the slot the caller asked for, because `parse_save_image` memsets the struct before extracting file bytes and `load_from_slot` never re-pinned the slot index. Mirroring the existing `theron_v1_save_import_slot` post-parse assignment now lets callers cross-check the slot they just loaded against the metadata they receive. Verification: direct binary PASS, focused Theron CTest sweep 31/31 green (no regressions), and broader `save_load|theron|tier1|tier2|tier4|v1-compatibility|v1` sweep 22/22 green. Source-locked against `include/theron_v1_save_load.h` (slotN.tqsv layout), `include/theron_v1_champions.h` (Theron_V1_Party + Theron_V1_Champion), `include/theron_v1_dungeon_progression.h`, THQUEST.ASM T080 (between-dungeon save/load), and THQUEST.ASM T800 (champion persistence between dungeons). Disjoint from `test_theron_v1_save_load` (dummy champion bytes) and `test_theron_v1_save_header_rejection` (mutated single header bytes). Documented in-file: map-level fields (`leader_x`/`leader_y`/`leader_dir`/`levitating`/`door_state_override`/`gold`) live in `Theron_V1_Party` outside the 4×`Theron_V1_Champion` pack stream and are not preserved by the current pack/unpack path; the test pins that documented behavior so a future struct-shape regression cannot silently start writing them into the pack stream without flagging the change.

## Dungeon Master Nexus

### Nexus V1

- ✅ Phase 0 - Provenance and source audit setup for Saturn DMDF/DGN references.
- ✅ Phase 1 - Runtime profile and launch/profile boundary scaffolding.
- ✅ Phase 2 - Data format ingestion for Nexus dungeon and supporting Saturn data structures.
- ✅ Phase 3 - Core world model and runtime state mapping.
- ✅ Phase 4 - Rendering pipeline slices and viewport/source-lock scaffolding.
- ✅ Phase 5 - Mechanics parity implementation for movement, click routing, item use, doors, pits, teleporters, triggers, combat, AI, and sound routes.
- ✅ Phase 6 - Save/import compatibility, including Nexus V1 save/load round-trip probe coverage.
- ✅ Phase 7 - Verification-suite coverage for compile, save/load, and runtime-state paths.
- ✅ 2026-06-22 DGN actor slot bounds gate: removed the dead hard-reject guard for OOB x/y/facing in `nexus_v1_creature_spawn` so the existing clamp/normalize path actually runs; out-of-range actor-type refs and the fixed active-pool boundary (ReDMCSB GROUP.C F0183) stay hard rejects. The data-free regression `tests/test_nexus_v1_dgn_actor_slot_bounds.c` is now wired into CMakeLists as CTest target `nexus_v1_dgn_actor_slot_bounds` and the focused parity probe `probes/nexus/firestaff_nexus_v1_mechanics_parity_probe.c::probe_dgn_actor_refs` was updated to the same clamp/reject contract. Verification: `ctest --test-dir build -R '^(nexus_v1_dgn_actor_slot_bounds|firestaff_nexus_v1_mechanics_parity)$' --output-on-failure` PASS 2/2; the 27-test Nexus ctest subset (`ctest --test-dir build -R nexus`) PASS 27/27 including `nexus_v1_dgn_actor_slot_bounds`, `firestaff_nexus_v1_mechanics_parity`, `nexus_v1_creature_state_determinism`, and `nexus_v2_*`; `git diff --check` clean. Source-lock comment in `nexus_v1_creatures.c` now cites the new test + probe and the active-pool boundary (GROUP.C F0183 lines 414-424 / 389-432). This is synthetic DGN actor-bound coverage only; real Saturn asset DGN handoff, original pixel parity, and broader runtime playability proof remain open.
- ✅ 2026-06-22 Nexus V1 DMDF embedded palette / string block bounds regression (parser-level): new `nexus_v1_dmdf_parse_palette_block` / `nexus_v1_dmdf_parse_string_block` / `nexus_v1_dmdf_palette_entry` / `nexus_v1_dmdf_string_record` helpers in `src/nexus/nexus_v1_dmdf_model.c` (declared in `include/nexus_v1_dmdf_model.h`) validate every offset, count and length against the caller-supplied (data, size) pair before any read, hard-cap entries to 256 with entry sizes {1, 2, 4} bytes (4bpp CLUT / BGR555 / 32-bit XRGB) and string records to 256 × 4-byte offsets / 4-byte lengths, and refuse to read past the declared block boundary. Output structs `Nexus_DMDFPaletteBlock` / `Nexus_DMDFStringBlock` expose `valid` so callers can branch safely. CTest `nexus_v1_dmdf_palette_bounds` 50/50 covers: canonical 256×BGR555 PLTB (Saturn VDP1 Color RAM), 16-entry 4bpp CLUT, 32-bit XRGB PLTB, 3-record STRB with shared-suffix records, truncated headers, oversize counts, length overflows, wrong magic, size mismatch, non-zero block offset, and full null-arg safety on all 4 entry points. Source-locked against docs/nexus_v1_phase2_data_formats_H2321.md §6.5 / §8.2 VDP1 BITMAP notes. Runtime handoff (per-cell palette lookup, texture decode) remains gated on real `.MNS` evidence.
- ✅ 2026-06-22 Nexus V1 save slot round-trip regression (single field): new `test_nexus_v1_save_slot_roundtrip_pc34_compat` CTest gates `nexus_v1_save_full()` -> `nexus_v1_load_full()` on slot 0 against a deterministic synthetic world + champion pool written to a private temp directory, with the single surviving gate field being `world.party_x` (set to PARTY_X_MARKER=17 via `nexus_v1_party_place` after `nexus_v1_world_init`, then rehydrated). Complementary slot-marker checks cover the cached `Nexus_V1_SaveSlot` header.party_x marker, the on-disk `nexus_save_00.dat` file presence, and the loaded `Nexus_V1_SaveHeader` (magic `FNXS`, version, party_x, current_level, data_size). Source-lock: `src/nexus/nexus_v1_save_load.c` manager API + `src/nexus/nexus_v1_world.c` party_x serialize/deserialize + ReDMCSB LOADSAVE.C F0433/F0434. CTest label: tier4;nexus;save_load. Disjoint from `test_nexus_v1_save_header_rejection` (malformed-magic rejection only), `test_nexus_v1_save_missing_root` (missing-root/non-launchable scan), and the existing `firestaff_nexus_v1_save_load_round_trip_probe` (writes the FNXS file by hand instead of using the high-level API).

### Nexus V2

- ✅ Phase 0 V1 compatibility lock + Phase 1 V2 launch/profile separation: `nexus_v2_phase_gate_pc34.c` (include/nexus_v2_phase_gate_pc34.h) introduces a 19-domain classification (11 V1-source-locked + 9 V2-presentation-eligible) with per-domain `NEXUS_V2_PhaseGateDecision` (v1SourceLocked, v2PresentationAllowed, sourceAnchor, rule). V1-locked domains (DMDF_DGN_LOADING, SATURN_ISO_READER, GAME_STATE_INIT, CHAMPION_PARTY, CREATURE_AI, SPELL_MAGIC, MOVEMENT, SAVE_LOAD, SOUND_DRIVER, RASTERIZER, INVENTORY) stay V1-locked regardless of V2 toggles. V2-eligible domains (RENDER_PRESENTATION, SMOOTH_MOVEMENT_PRESENTATION, DYNAMIC_LIGHTING_PRESENTATION, HUD_OVERLAY, PARTICLE_EFFECTS, ATMOSPHERE, INPUT_PRESENTATION, CONFIG_PRESENTATION, UPSCALER) require v2PresentationEnabled=1; CONFIG_PRESENTATION additionally requires v2ConfigPersistenceEnabled=1 (stricter gate because config writes are persistent). Default config: V1-only, both toggles off. Ctest target `test_nexus_v2_phase_gate_pc34` passes 240/240 (defaults, null-args, V1/V2-on behaviour, CONFIG-persistence, v2_active, all 20 domain names, source-evidence, all-domain anchor, unknown-domain safety). Headless probe `firestaff_nexus_v2_phase0_v1_compatibility_lock_probe` passes 218/218 (same invariants, source-evidence citation). Headless probe `firestaff_nexus_v2_phase1_launch_profile_separation_probe` passes 60/60 (launch gate, profile gate, Nexus V1 asset hash separation for 0DMSTRT.BIN/DM.BIN/LEV00.DGN/LEV15.DGN/ITEM.IBS/FACE.BIN/FILE_LISTING.txt, cross-game hash separation Nexus≠DM1≠CSB, V1-only default, headless safety). Source-locked against NEXUS.C / NEXUS2.C / NEXUS.BIN, nexus_v1_iso_reader.c, nexus_v1_dmdf_model.c, nexus_v1_dungeon.c, nexus_v1_engine.c, nexus_v1_game.c, nexus_v1_champions.c, nexus_v1_creatures.c, nexus_v1_movement.c, nexus_v1_combat.c, nexus_v1_magic.c, nexus_v1_inventory.c, nexus_v1_save_load.c, nexus_v1_sound.c, nexus_v1_rasterizer.c, ReDMCSB CLIKMENU.C:142/180 F0365/F0366, COMMAND.C:2045 F0380, MOVESENS.C:316-345 F0267, HuC6260/HuC6270 VDC/VCE, THQUEST.ASM T400-T900, scripts/fixtures/nexus_v1_disc_file_hashes.py (138-file SHA256 table).
- ✅ Phase 2 Enhanced asset pipeline (V2.1 part): `nexus_v2_upscaler.c` (include/nexus_v2_upscaler.h) provides the EPX/Scale2x upscaler for Nexus V2.1, mirroring DM1 V2.1 (same algorithm). `nexus_v2_epx_upscale(src, src_w, src_h, dst, dst_w, dst_h, palette)` converts V1 indexed pixels (0..255) through a 256-entry palette to RGBA. `nexus_v2_bilinear_smooth(buf, w, h)` is the optional post-filter. `nexus_v2_upscaler_source_evidence()` cites DM1 V2.1 EPX implementation + Scale2x algorithm + Saturn VDP1 bitmap upscaling + ReDMCSB GFX.C. Headless probe `firestaff_nexus_v2_upscaler_probe` passes 23/23 (palette lookup with all dst pixels matching a palette entry, deterministic for same input, 2x scaling fills all dst pixels with no 0xCC sentinel left, 1x1 boundary case maps to palette[src[0]] in all 4 output pixels, null-arg safety on src/dst/palette + zero-dims, bilinear null-arg safety on null/0x0/1x1/4x4, source evidence). Ctest `nexus_v2_upscaler_probe` 1/1. The V2.2 modern asset pack (per-cell V22 art swap) is still TODO and is the remaining Phase 2 work.

New `m11_high_contrast_overlay_pc34_compat` module (header + src) owns the M11-side gate state sourced from `M12_Config.highContrast`. The launcher pushes the same config bit into `M11_HighContrast_SetActive()` from `m12_apply_loaded_config()` (`src/ui/menu_startup_m12.c`) right after the existing `M11_UIScale_SetPercent` / `M11_Ambient_SetEnabled` push, so the in-game chrome uses the same restricted palette as the launcher when the toggle is on. The 320x200 dungeon-viewport pixel data and the HUD panel C040 / C017 backdrop blits are deliberately preserved bit-exact because raw viewport pixels are painted via separate bitmap-blit paths (`m11_draw_viewport`, the per-cell wall/floor/door/creature blits) and never go through `m11_draw_text`. `M11_HighContrast_ApplyActiveRGBA()` exposes a region apply with a 16-bit `excludeMask` so callers can fence off the dungeon-viewport subrect even on chrome overlays; `M11_HighContrast_GetManifest()` returns a stable, parseable string documenting the coverage / preserve / default-state contract. New CTest `m11_high_contrast_overlay_pc34_compat` PASS 369/369 (default-off identity, toggle round-trip, restricted-palette remap when on with full 0..255 input sweep, manifest string contract, region apply gate off → no-op, region apply gate on with no exclude, region apply gate on with excludeMask, region clipping with negative origin / over-large rect / zero-area / NULL fb / zero dimensions, out-of-range index handling under excludeMask, launcher / game palette parity). New headless probe `firestaff_m11_high_contrast_overlay_runtime_probe` PASS 14/14 (default-off state, launcher-config-driven gate push, chrome remap under gate, simulated 320x200 viewport fence preserving dungeon scene, HUD chrome strip remap outside the fence, toggle round-trip restores V1 identity, manifest documents gap closure). Registered as `m11_high_contrast_overlay_pc34_compat` + `m11_high_contrast_overlay_runtime_probe` with labels `tier2;m11;accessibility;high-contrast`. Source-lock: none required — pure accessibility glue that mirrors the existing `m12_presented_color()` contract in `src/ui/menu_startup_m12.c` and adds the in-game counterpart; ReDMCSB does not cover high-contrast palette remap. **2026-06-28 rectangle-fence apply helper hardened the viewport fence:** new `M11_HighContrast_ApplyActiveRGBAExceptRect()` exposes the explicit rectangle-fence variant of the region apply so a broad chrome-overlay pass can skip a precise dungeon-viewport rectangle (e.g. `0,0,224,136` over the 320x200 logical buffer) instead of relying only on palette-index `excludeMask` bit-fencing. The fence is evaluated BEFORE `excludeMask`, so a muted palette index inside the preserve rectangle is NEVER touched (the original dungeon scene stays bit-identical even when those pixels would otherwise collapse to BLACK); pixels outside the preserve rectangle still follow the restricted-palette remap. A non-positive `preserveWidth` / `preserveHeight` disables the rectangle fence and falls back to the existing `excludeMask`-only contract. The new helper is wired into a shared `m11_high_contrast_apply_active_region()` static implementation so the original `M11_HighContrast_ApplyActiveRGBA()` retains its `excludeMask`-only contract unchanged (callers that pass `0,0,0,0` for the preserve rectangle get identical behavior). Manifest string gets the new `chrome_rect_remap_with_viewport_fence` coverage token so downstream tools can audit the new helper by name. New CTest `m11_high_contrast_overlay_pc34_compat` PASS 379/379 (the original 369 + 10 new rectangle-fence assertions covering broad remap reports chrome changes, preserve rectangle stays byte-identical, chrome outside the rectangle follows the remap table, zero-area preserve rect disables the rectangle fence and falls back to excludeMask, negative preserve dimension disables the rectangle fence, gate off leaves every pixel alone even with a real preserve rect, manifest coverage entry). Headless probe `firestaff_m11_high_contrast_overlay_runtime_probe` PASS 19/19 (the original 14 + 5 new invariants covering rect-fenced broad remap touches HUD chrome strip, rect-fenced broad remap preserves dungeon viewport pixels, rect-fenced broad remap collapses chrome strip to BLACK, zero-area preserve rect disables the rectangle fence, rect-fence helper preserves checker pattern inside the dungeon viewport). The `m11_ui_scale`, `m11_phase_a`, and `m11_session_timer_runtime` CTest targets still PASS unchanged. `git diff --check` clean; `-Wall -Wextra -O2` clean on every new + touched file. Pins the documented "out of scope" fallthrough contract for the 12 launcher views that intentionally fall through to `emit_main_view` as a navigation anchor: `M12_MENU_VIEW_DATA_VALIDATOR` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_AUDIO_SETTINGS` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_ACCESSIBILITY` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_THEME` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_SAVE_BROWSER` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_INPUT_REMAP` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_CUSTOM_DUNGEON` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_CAMPAIGN` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_SPELL_REFERENCE` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_MAP_VIEWER` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_TOUCH_LAYOUT` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_PRESENTATION_PREVIEW`. For each of the 12 views, the subtest asserts (a) the envelope `gameState` matches the active view (`launcher_<viewName>` — screen reader can announce "launcher theme" instead of "launcher main"), (b) the `GAME_CARD_DM1` / `MENU_SETTINGS` / `MENU_MUSEUM` / `GAME_CARD_THERON` navigation anchors are emitted, (c) the framebuffer dims stay pinned to 480x270, and (d) no foreign view markers leak into the manifest (the forbidden-marker table covers `ROW_*`, `TAB_*`, `CHANGELOG_LINE_*`, `MANUAL_DOC_*`, `BESTIARY_CAT_*`, `BESTIARY_ROW_*`, `ITEM_CAT_*`, `ITEM_ROW_*`, `SCREENSHOT_ROW_*`, `MUSEUM_CATEGORY_*`, `MUSEUM_BULLET_*`, `POPUP_MESSAGE`, `POPUP_OK`, `POPUP_LINE*`). The leak marker is printed in the probe log so a regression report tells the operator exactly which view-family leaked. The probe grew from 91/91 PASS to 175/175 PASS (84 new invariants, 7 per view × 12 views). The subtest is header-driven from a small `FallthroughViewSpec` table so adding the 13th view only takes one row. A future dedicated emitter for any of these 12 views only needs to assert that the new view-specific markers appear AND the fallthrough markers disappear — the navigation-anchor contract is already pinned. Source-lock: none required — pure accessibility/automation contract on top of public launcher state, same scope as the existing launcher manifest probe. ReDMCSB does not cover the launcher.

- ✅ 2026-06-17 DM2 CLI launch fix: closed the documented "direct launch failed for --game dm2" gap. **Bug 1 (M11 launch path missing):** `M11_GameView_Start` previously had no DM2 branch and fell through to the DM1 dungeon loader which tried to parse DM2's DUNGEON.DAT as DM1 format. Added a DM2 branch that scans assets in `data_dir/dm2/` (with fallback to root), calls `dm2_v1_boot_enter_game()` to allocate the DM2 V1 game state, initializes the DM2 V2 runtimes (runtime + HUD + touch), and sets `state->sourceKind = M11_GAME_SOURCE_DM2_BOOT`. The M11 per-frame tick + render dispatch on `M11_GAME_SOURCE_DM2_BOOT` (already present) now drives the DM2 V1 runtime via `dm2_v1_runtime_tick()`. **Bug 2 (DM2 V1 boot MD5 wrong):** `dm2_md5_body` had two bugs that silently produced wrong hashes — (a) trailing `+ a` on each line was adding the wrong variable (should be `+ b` for the a-line, `+ c` for the b-line, etc.), and (b) F/G/H/I argument order was wrong on 3 of 4 lines per cycle (the OTHER three variables in cyclic order, not always starting with the same variable). Rewrote the body using the STEP macro form from `src/shared/asset_find_by_hash.c` (verified to match RFC 1321 test vectors: `d41d8cd9...` for empty, `90015098...` for "abc"). **Verification:** Re-ran `/tmp/firestaff-launch-verify/verify_all_launches.sh` — DM2 default + scale 0-3 + 4 resolution variants all PASS (was FAIL_NODATA for all 10). ctest 487/487 green (excluded 4 pre-existing DM1 V1 parity-blockers). Phase A 23/23.

- ✅ 2026-06-19 pass841 (FTL swoosh 4bpp-packed buffer treated as 1-byte-per-pixel — user-reported v2.9.0 macOS arm64 regression): the FTL swoosh intro animation displayed as a half-blank vertically-striped image on Apple Silicon because `SWSH_Compat_ExpandLogoToBitmap` writes Atari ST low-res 4bpp-packed (32000 bytes, 2 pixels/byte) into a buffer the runtime treats as 1-byte-per-pixel indexed (64000 bytes). Pixels 160..319 of every row stayed zero (logo only rendered in the left half) and even pixels 0..159 showed alternating nibbles (vertical stripes). Fix: new helper `m11_swsh_unpack_4bpp_to_indexed` in `src/engine/main_loop_m11.c` (mirrors the existing `m11_unpack_title_4bpp_to_indexed` already used by the DM title path); dedicated 32000-byte packed buffer for SWSH expansion, then unpack into 64000-byte indexed buffer before palette/RGBA conversion. Also removed dead `paletteDirty` flag in `m11_play_ftl_swoosh_if_available` (was initialized to 0, never set to 1, so the WAIT_VBLANKS `if (paletteDirty) render` branch was unreachable). Source-lock against ReDMCSB Atari ST VDI / LINEA F0080_vq_extend / F0086_vs_clip low-res Physbase layout. Verification: `probes/v1/firestaff_v1_ftl_swoosh_palette_regression_probe.c` — 9/9 invariants incl. F841_SWSH_BUG_PACKED_DETECTED + F841_SWSH_UNPACK_VALID + F841_SWSH_UNPACK_COVERAGE + 4 load-bearing palette invariants; pre-fix sha256 `56549f3a...` post-fix `6612c1b1...`. ASCII companion `probes/v1/firestaff_v1_ftl_swoosh_ascii_probe.c` dumps the unpacked logo for eyeball regression check. CTest: `ftl_swoosh_palette_regression` + `ftl_swoosh_ascii_sanity` PASS, full suite 699/699 green (was 692/696 before parity-evidence watchdog churn unrelated to this fix).
